WAS MADE THEREIN AS UNDER:
CORAM: HON'BLE MRS JUSTICE M G UMA  ORAL ORDER Petitioners being accused Nos.7, 8 and 9 in Cr.No.34/2018 of Vidyaranyapura Police Station now pending before IV Addl.Chief Metropolitan Magistrate, Bengaluru, for the offences punishable under Section 3 and 4 of Dowry Prohibition Act, 1961, under Sections 354(1) (ii) & (iii), 494, 504,
506, 498A r/w Section 149 I.P.C are before this Court, seeking quashing of the criminal proceedings initiated against them.
NC: 2024:KHC:40526 2.

The brief facts of the case are that, the informant - respondent No.2 filed the First Information with Vidyaranyapura Police Station against accused Nos.1 to 9 alleging commission of aforesaid offences.
It is contended that accused No.1 is her husband, accused No.2 is his brother, accused Nos.3 and 4 are the parents and accused Nos.5 and 6 are the relatives of accused No.1.
It is specifically contended that accused No.1 married accused No.9 during the subsistence of marriage of respondent No.2 and accused No.1.
It is stated that accused Nos.7 and 8 are the parents of accused No.9 and it is alleged that they have committed offences under Section 494 of I.P.C.
The petitioners being accused Nos.7 to 9 are seeking to quash the criminal proceedings initiated against them.
3. Heard Sri.Harish Kumar M.S, learned counsel for petitioners and Smt.Asma Kouser, Addl.SPP for respondent No.1.
Perused the material placed on record.

sentences.text:
In view of the rival contentions urged by the learned counsel for both the parties, the point that would arise for my consideration is:
 "Whether the petitioners have  made out any grounds to allow the  petition?"
5.

My answer to the above point is in 'Affirmative' for the following:
REASONS 6.
It is the contention of the petitioner that they are arraigned as accused Nos.7 to 9.
It is alleged that accused No.9 is the second wife of accused No.1 and accused Nos.7 and 8 are the parents of accused No.9.
Thus they have committed the offence under Section 494 of I.P.C.

As per prosecution,
since such allegations are made against accused No.1, these petitioners are liable for prosecution under Section 494 or 495 of I.P.C.
7.

Learned counsel for the petitioners places reliance on the decision of Hon'ble Apex Court in NC:
2024:KHC:40526 S.Nitheen and Ors. Vs. State of Kerala and Anr.,1 wherein the Hon'ble Apex Court referred to its earlier decision in Gopal Lal V. State of Rajasthan2, held in para Nos.14 to 16 as under:
"14.

sentences.text: At the outset, we may note that the complaint was filed alleging commission of the offence punishable under Section 494 read with Section 34 IPC.

However, post recording pre-charge evidence, the learned JMFC passed an order dated 28th May,
2018 directing framing of charge against all the accused persons for the offence punishable under Section 494 IPC.
15.

The essential ingredients of offence under Section 494 IPC, as explained by this Court in the case of Gopal V. State of Rajasthan, are as follows:
"3. The essential ingredients of this office are: (1) that the accused spouse must have contracted the first marriage.

(2) that while the first marriage was subsisting the spouse concerned must have contracted a second marriage, and (3) that both the marriages must be valid in the sense that the necessary ceremonies required by the personal law governing the parties had been duly performed

A bare perusal of the penal provision would indicate that the order framing charge is erroneous on the face of the record because no person other than the spouse to the second marriage could have been charged for the offence punishable under Section 494 IPC simplicitor.
However, this is a curable defect, and the charge can be altered at any stage as per the provisions of Section 216 CrPC."
(emphasis supplied)
8. Thus the position of law is well settled.

When it is the specific contention of petitioner No.3 that respondent No.1/accused No.1 being her husband, contracted second marriage, hence, it is accused No.1 who is alone liable for prosecution under Section 494 I.P.C.
These petitioners who are said to be the second wife and her parents are not liable to be prosecuted.

When admittedly there are no other allegations against these petitioners except for the offence punishable under Section 494 I.P.C,
I am of the considered opinion that criminal proceedings initiated against them is liable to be quashed.

9. Accordingly, I proceed to pass the following:
NC: 2024:KHC:40526 ORDER Criminal Petition is allowed.
The First Information Report dated 05.02.2018 (Document No.1) in Cr.No.34/2018 of Vidyaranyapura Police Station, Bengaluru, on the file of IV Addl.Chief Metropolitan Magistrate, Bengaluru, is hereby quashed against the petitioners.
Since criminal petition is disposed off, pending interlocutory application (I.A.No.1/2022), does not survive for consideration and the same is disposed off.

SD/-
